sections.heading: Before or After Your Delivery Order

blocks.html: Leonia earned its nickname, the Athens of New Jersey, honestly. The borough has been drawing artists, intellectuals, and community-minded residents to its tree-lined streets since the late 1800s, and that creative energy hasn't faded. Broad Avenue runs through the heart of the commercial district; Hillside Avenue adds its own quieter character; and the residential blocks between Fort Lee Road and Christie Heights Street give the borough the kind of settled, walkable feel that's hard to manufacture. Weed delivery Leonia residents rely on from Lady L means your plans stay on your terms, whether you'll be heading out to spend time in town or relaxing at home for the rest of the day.

blocks.title: Erika and David Boyd Sculpture Garden
blocks.html: The Erika and David Boyd Sculpture Garden at Broad Avenue and Beechwood Place is an outdoor exhibition space maintained by Sculpture for Leonia, an all-volunteer nonprofit founded in 2008. Works by artists from around the world are displayed on rotating loans, with some pieces donated permanently to the borough. Additional sculptures installed through the program can be found at the public library and in local parks. The organization's annual Taste of Leonia fundraiser, held each fall in the garden, brings together food, wine, live music, and a silent auction in one of the borough's most distinctive public spaces.

blocks.title: Civil War Drill Hall Theatre
blocks.html: Built in 1859 at 130 Grand Avenue, the Civil War Drill Hall is home to the Players Guild of Leonia, founded in 1919 and recognized as New Jersey's oldest continuing community theater group. The guild grew out of the same creative spirit that made Leonia a destination for artists across three generations, and it has maintained an unbroken run of community productions ever since. Five minutes from the George Washington Bridge, the theater draws audiences from well beyond the borough for its annual season of plays and musicals performed entirely by local talent.

blocks.title: Wood Park
blocks.html: Wood Park at 370 Broad Avenue is Leonia's most fully equipped public park, with three tennis courts, a tennis wall, basketball courts, a softball field, multiple picnic areas, and a shelter house with restrooms. The park shares a parking lot with the Leonia Public Library on Fort Lee Road, making it a natural anchor for the borough's civic and recreational life. Mature trees and open lawns give it a quiet, unhurried character that draws residents year-round.

blocks.title: Leonia Public Library
blocks.html: The Leonia Public Library is one of the more fully featured public libraries in the area for its size. Beyond a strong circulating collection, it offers a Library of Things that includes board games, mobile hotspots, classic video games, and electronics kits, along with 3D printing access, ESL classes, tech assistance appointments, museum passes, a seed library, and a digital collection spanning Libby, Hoopla, Kanopy, and Mango language learning. The library also hosts rotating monthly art exhibitions, a nod to the borough's deep creative roots.

blocks.title: Choo Choo Train Sushi
blocks.html: Choo Choo Train at 374 Broad Avenue is a conveyor belt sushi restaurant built around a train-themed concept that's as much about the experience as the food. A miniature train delivers dishes directly to tables, while a full menu of specialty rolls and à la carte selections ensures there's something for every preference. The kitchen consistently produces highly rated sushi with creative rolls, fresh ingredients, and vegan options alongside traditional offerings, earning the restaurant a loyal following along Leonia's main commercial corridor.

blocks.title: Rumba Cafe
blocks.html: Rumba Cafe on Hillside Avenue serves authentic Colombian and Cuban cuisine in a warm, no-frills setting that regulars return for specifically because of the quality of the cooking. The menu centers on traditional recipes made with fresh ingredients, with standout dishes including ajiaco, a rich traditional Colombian soup; bandeja paisa; coconut rice; Cuban sandwiches; and freshly made tostones. It's the kind of neighborhood spot that builds its reputation one honest plate at a time.

items.q: What's the most cannabis I can order at one time in Leonia?
items.a_html:
New Jersey caps each transaction at one ounce, or 28.35 grams, of usable cannabis. That ceiling covers all product types combined, broken down as follows:

  • Dried Flower/Bud: 28.35 grams (1 ounce).
  • Concentrates/Resin/Oils: 4 grams (solid or liquid/vaporized oil).
  • Ingestible Items (Gummies/Edibles): 1,000 mg of THC (roughly ten 100mg packages).
  • Maximum Possession Limit: Up to 6 ounces of cannabis and cannabis products.
  • Mixing Products: You can mix and match, for example, by purchasing 1/2 ounce of flower and 2 grams of concentrates.
  • Daily Limits: The 1-ounce limit is generally considered a daily limit across all dispensaries.

items.q: Are there taxes on cannabis delivery orders in Leonia?
items.a_html: Yes, and they're straightforward. New Jersey applies a 6.625% state sales tax, a $2.50-per-ounce Social Equity Excise Fee (SEEF), and a 2% municipal transfer or user tax in municipalities that have authorized it. Every charge is itemized at checkout before you confirm, so you know exactly what you're paying before you commit.
